title: Man. Post. Cap. X: GAR.2 — same duration logic would also bar imputing Christ’s actual obedience
pass_a_gloss: Garissoles’ second thrust: the duration argument used against imputing Adam’s sin could as well be used against imputing Christ’s actual obedience—if Adam’s disobedience was not imputed until the law because it did not last until the law, why may one not also say Christ’s obedience unto death cannot be imputed to us because it did not last until our times?
pass_b_english: GAR. 2. The argument which is here used against the imputation of Adam’s sin, someone could use no less against the imputation of Christ’s actual obedience.

For if it is rightly gathered that Adam’s disobedience was not imputed until the law, because it did not endure until the law: why may it not also be legitimately gathered that Christ’s actual obedience, by which he showed himself obedient unto death, can in no way be imputed to us, because it did not last until our times?
source_text: GAR. 2. Argumento quod hic usurpatur adversus imputationem peccati Adae, non minus uti poterit aliquis adversus imputationem actualis obedientiae Christi. Nam si recte colligitur inobedientiam Adami non fuisse imputatam usque ad legem, quia non perduravit usque ad legem: quidni etiam legitime colligatur, actualem Christi obedientiam, qua se obedientem praestitit usque ad mortem, nobis nequaquam imputari posse, quia non duravit usque ad nostra tempora?

lemmas.latin: usque ad legem / usque ad nostra tempora
lemmas.gloss: until the law / until our times

choices.choice: Duration logic would also bar Christ’s obedience-imputation
